summary.text: The Schrödinger equation is a partial differential equation that governs the wave function of a non-relativistic quantum system, and it was a landmark in the development of quantum mechanics.
It is the quantum counterpart of Newton's second law, giving how a system's wave function changes over time instead of a path.
Erwin Schrödinger postulated it in 1925 from de Broglie's idea of matter waves and published it in 1926, and it predicted the atom's bound states in agreement with experiments.

facts.label: Namesake
facts.value: Erwin Schrödinger, an Austrian physicist, who won the 1933 Nobel Prize

facts.label: Based on
facts.value: De Broglie's postulate that all matter has an associated wave

facts.label: Alternatives
facts.value: Matrix mechanics and the path integral formulation

facts.label: Relativistic fix
facts.value: Dirac's equation includes special relativity and reduces to Schrödinger's

items.prompt: Newton's second law predicts a ball's path from its starting conditions. What does the Schrödinger equation predict from a starting wave function?

options.label: The ball's exact path
How the wave function evolves over time
The ball's color at each moment
Which equation to use next

items.explain: It is the quantum counterpart of Newton's second law, giving the time evolution of the wave function of an isolated system.

items.prompt: What idea did Schrödinger build on when writing his equation?

options.label: That all matter has an associated matter wave
That light travels in perfectly straight lines
That atoms cannot be split apart
That the Sun orbits the Earth

items.explain: The equation was postulated based on Louis de Broglie's postulate of a matter wave for all matter.

items.prompt: A friend says the Schrödinger equation is the only way to do quantum mechanics. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, no other method has ever been developed
Yes, but only for photons
No, but the others give results only on paper
No, matrix mechanics and path integrals are other formulations

items.explain: Other formulations include Heisenberg's matrix mechanics and Feynman's path integral formulation.

items.prompt: Why is the Schrödinger equation called non-relativistic?

options.label: It only works for objects sitting at rest
Time and space enter unequally, once versus twice
It was published before Einstein's work
It ignores energy altogether in its terms

items.explain: Because it has a first time derivative and a second space derivative, space and time are not on equal footing.

items.prompt: After the equation, a relativistic wave equation gave a probability density that could go negative. Who fixed this and how?

options.label: Schrödinger, by dropping the wave function
Heisenberg, by removing probability from the theory
Dirac, by introducing Dirac matrices
Feynman, by adding more particles

items.explain: The Klein-Gordon equation's negative probability density was fixed by Dirac with Dirac matrices.

items.prompt: When an observable is measured, what are the possible results?

options.label: Any number at all, with equal odds
Only the number zero, every time
One of its eigenvalues, by Born-rule odds
Only whole numbers, never fractions

items.explain: The result will be one of the observable's eigenvalues, with probability given by the Born rule.
